olivia: Quick report — users on Android 12 hitting a token refresh loop when the device enters Doze. Behavior: app backgrounded, network gated, then when network returns we see a flurry of 401s and repeated refreshes.

sam: Is this the same issue as interceptor order (auth interceptor after retry interceptor)?

olivia: Sort of. In our SDK the Retry interceptor runs before the Auth interceptor for non-idempotent calls because we attached it as an application interceptor. On reconnect, OkHttp retries the call and the auth interceptor sees an unauthenticated request and triggers refresh multiple times.

kai: Can you paste the interceptor chain config?

olivia: Our builder: ```kotlin
OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(retryInterceptor) // app-level
  .addNetworkInterceptor(authInterceptor)
  .build()
```

mike: Hmm the retryInterceptor should be a network interceptor or should run after auth. Also token refresh should be single-flight.

olivia: We implemented single-flight but the race happens because the retry creates fresh Calls that bypass the in-flight map briefly. The in-flight key is on the request URI + body hash; retries recreate body streams and the key mismatches.

sam: Short-term fix: make auth interceptor an application interceptor and do single-flight keyed by refresh token or account id rather than request body. That way retries map to same refresh op.

kai: Also consider marking non-idempotent requests as not retryable during network flaps. We can tune RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor config.

mike: Can we add a small unit test simulating Doze reconnects? Use robolectric + fake connectivity toggles and assert only one refresh call per user. Owner: mike?

mike: I'll add a test and a small patch to change in-flight key to (userId|refreshToken) and flip auth interceptor ordering. Will open PR.

ci-bot: Created ticket sdk-android#512 "android: doze reconnect causes multiple token refreshes due to interceptor ordering" and attached logs (assigned to @mike).

olivia: Thanks. I'll add a note to mobile onboarding docs advising integrators to prefer token-based single-flight and to avoid body-based keys for retries.

sam: Nice catch. emoji: :raised_hands:
